name: Al-Khāzinī’s Balance of Wisdom
description: Treatise combining balance theory and comparative measurement of material weights.

impact.note: One treatise refining the hydrostatic balance and specific-weight tables of earlier scholars; known to a small circle with few traced successors.

date.label: 1121–1122 CE
date.basis: Historical literature places completion in 515 AH, corresponding to 1121–1122; not a dated surviving manuscript or manufacturing day.

events.statement: Al-Khāzinī’s Book of the Balance of Wisdom described the science of weights and a refined hydrostatic balance in Merv.

evidence.supports: Discusses the book, Merv, balances and predecessor work.

evidence.locator: The claim and its basis; The story
evidence.supports: Dates the treatise 1121–1122 and distinguishes earlier balance designs.

contributions.resource: Developed or authored the described account.

evidence.supports: Discusses the book, Merv, balances and predecessor work.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated source-bounded episode in this record, not a claim of worldwide priority.

caveats: Al-Asfizari and other predecessors contributed balance designs and concepts; descriptions do not establish a mass-produced instrument or date its manufacture. Scholarly descriptions differ over attribution. The 1859/1860 English analysis contains extracts rather than a complete translation.

research.note: Chronology distinguishes composition or formulation from later surviving textual witnesses. Independent review checked the event dating and scope against the cited work, historical source, edition metadata or modern translation, as applicable.

places.note: Merv is the place of the treatise according to the historical account.
